title: What Blind People Dream, Ask, and What AI Tells Them: A Public-Data Study of Sensory Mediation in the AI Age
motivation: This public-data study connects historical blind dream expression, BLV-originating information-seeking questions, human accessibility references, and the information made available by a frozen multimodal AI system. It tests a prompt intervention on model output while separating distributional comparison from claims about cognition or lived experience.
method_scope: We analyze released research datasets and a frozen within-item VLM intervention with no new human data collection. Synthetic annotations are computational measurements, not human judgments; released human-labelled datasets provide bounded external calibration only where their labels directly support the construct.
impact_scope: The paper discusses design implications for how systems expose task-relevant, spatial, uncertainty, and social information. It does not report perceived benefit, lived experience, measured harm, cognitive change, or a dream effect.
